metadata.title: The Number Went Up.
metadata.clock: narration (Kokoro af_bella) - per-beat mp3 durations are MEASURED, never estimated
metadata.greeting_note: hello lexicon. SKILL.md limits the HAI persona to the SHORTEST forms only (Hi / Ola / Hej / Ciao) so the serif line stays one comfortable line. Ep. 03 Hej, Ep. 04 Ciao, Ep. 05 Ola, Ep. 06 Salut, Ep. 07 Namaste - which was outside HAI's permitted set. Ep. 08 uses the one remaining legal form, Hi.
metadata.target_runtime: Under 3:00 BY DESIGN. 434 words against Ep. 07's measured 0.3843 s/word predicts 2:46.8, leaving 13.2 s of margin. The human asked for under three minutes on Ep. 06; from Ep. 07 onward the script is SIZED before it is written, never trimmed after signature. The margin is deliberately wider than Ep. 07's 9.8 s because the words-only model UNDER-predicts spoken numerals - Ep. 06 predicted 2:50 and measured 3:07.7 - and this script is numeral-heavy. A first draft came in at 454 words (2:54.5 predicted); six lines were cut BEFORE GATE P, moving four figures off the voice and onto the screen, which SHOW-DON'T-TELL wanted anyway.
metadata.purpose: Ep. 08 of the AI in Astronomy & Space Science series, from weekly_stem_videos/ideas.md Astronomy topic 08 (Asteroid/comet tracking - automated detection and orbit prediction for planetary defence, NASA's ATLAS system).
metadata.color_semantics: Claude fidelity palette. Terracotta #D97757 is the ONE accent and marks WHAT THE MACHINE DECIDES throughout - the detections the network calls real, the two real postage-stamp classes, the fitted tracklet, the uncertainty cloud, the impact-probability curve. Ink marks WHAT THE SKY ACTUALLY DOES - the Earth, the capture disc, the catalogued fraction. The mapping is fixed for the whole reel, so B04 teaches it once and every later plate reads for free. Accented text is #A44A32; #B9B4A0 is strokes and fills only. Sky frames are warm bright-on-dark; plots and diagrams are ink-on-white.
metadata.distinct_from_earlier_episodes: Eps. 01-06 had AI inspecting observations; Ep. 07 had AI standing in for a calculation. Ep. 08 is the first episode about a DIVISION OF LABOUR: the learned part and the computed part sit in the same pipeline, and the number that frightens people comes from the computed half. The limit is therefore new - not an accuracy ceiling (Ep. 04), an unseen class (Ep. 03), an irreversible rejection (Ep. 05), a latency (Ep. 06) or a circularity (Ep. 07), but a MISREADING: a rising probability is evidence that the uncertainty is shrinking, not that the danger grew.
metadata.note: ILLUSTRATE LAW: the Claude UI appears at B00, B11, B12, B13. Every other beat illustrates its concept as a reel-local Manim scene (scenes.py). All plates come from assets/gen_neo.py, which RUNS the calculations the episode describes - real image differencing, the eight artefact classes each synthesised from its own physical model, a least-squares tracklet fit, and a target-plane quadrature for the impact probability. That last one ASSERTS its own analytic peak (sigma -> d/sqrt(2)) and refuses to write a plate if it disagrees. PUBLISHED numbers and COMPUTED-HERE numbers are kept apart on screen and in the narration: B07 and B09 quote the real 2024 YR4 record, B08 shows this reel's own computation of why that record had the shape it did. No published figure is reproduced or redrawn. No LaTeX/MathTex anywhere. metadata.channel_title is omitted for the GATE V edge-bleed reason logged in Ep. 03. scenes.py is ASPECT-AWARE: one file lays out 16:9 and the 9:16 derivative in short/.

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Om Mali. This video is about how sky surveys and a neural network find asteroids headed for Earth, and why a rising chance of impact is usually the system working.

show.event: cream page; IRREDUCIBLY HUMAN eyebrow, then the serif segment title
spark + greeting Hi, HAI settles above the composer card
the ask types itself into the composer; send button arms when it lands
terracotta running indicator: screening 100,000 alerts...
three result lines stagger in - detect, decide, limit. The ask lands ANSWERED.

props.command: An asteroid's impact odds climbed to three percent, then fell to zero. What actually finds these objects, which part of that is machine learning, and why did the number rise before it collapsed?
output: detect - a CNN sorts eight kinds of dot: 99.6% on real asteroids, 90% less to screen
decide - the probability is not learned. It is two-hundred-year-old celestial mechanics
limit - eleven impactors ever caught in advance; 40% of the 140-metre class found

beats.narration_text: Seven episodes of AI reading the sky. This one is about the moment the reading stops and the arithmetic starts.

show.event: OM MALI writes in, terracotta hairline underlines it
role line fades in beneath: Humanitarians AI - presenter
a card draws beside it
row one lands and is STRUCK: seven episodes / AI reads the sky
row two lands in the accent and is boxed: this one / the reading ends, the arithmetic begins
closer: Ep. 08 - the number is not the news

beats.narration_text: Telescopes sweep the whole sky every night. A network throws out the junk so people only look at plausible rocks. Then celestial mechanics decides whether to worry, and that number can rise for a good reason.

show.event: a wide star-field frame lands, captioned as a synthetic toy field
kinetic type set one: THE SKY IS SCANNED NIGHTLY
set two replaces it: A NETWORK REMOVES THE JUNK
set three lands in the accent: ARITHMETIC DECIDES
closer: finding it is learned. fearing it is not.

beats.narration_text: Four telescopes photograph the same field four times a night, then subtract last night's picture. What is left is anything that moved, plus cosmic rays, satellites, and every star the subtraction got slightly wrong.

show.event: two sky frames land side by side, labelled last night and tonight
the third panel arrives: their difference, ink on cream
a terracotta ring closes on the one real mover in the difference
a chip lands: about 100,000 alerts a night
closer: most of what moves is not a rock

beats.narration_text: The first stage is a convolutional network, and its whole job is telling eight kinds of dot apart. A cosmic ray is one pixel. A bad subtraction is two lobes. Only two are real.

show.event: the eight postage stamps land as a grid, two rows of four
each stamp's class name types in beneath it
the cosmic-ray stamp is ringed - one pixel, no point-spread function
the dipole stamp is ringed - a positive and a negative lobe
the two REAL classes take terracotta rules; the six artefacts stay ghost
closer: it learns what the camera lies about

beats.narration_text: Then a second network reads four detections in a row. A real rock walks a straight line at a steady rate; junk does not. That cut what humans must screen by ninety percent.

show.event: four terracotta dots land on a field, one per exposure
a terracotta line is fitted through them - straight, constant rate
four hollow dots scatter in: unrelated artefacts, no line fits them
counters run up: 99.6% on real asteroids, 0.4% false negatives
the third counter lands in the accent: 90% less to screen
closer: the point was speed, not cleverness

beats.narration_text: Now the network is done. It never learned an orbit. What happens next is much older arithmetic: fit a trajectory, then sample every orbit the data still allows. That cloud is the answer.

show.event: two boxes draw side by side
box one fills terracotta: LEARNED - is this dot real?
box two fills ink: COMPUTED - where does it go?
an arrow runs from the first to the second; the terracotta stops at the boundary
beneath, a cloud of sampled orbits fans out from one fitted track
closer: it never computes a risk

beats.narration_text: In December, a survey telescope in Chile caught a sixty-metre rock. Its odds of hitting Earth climbed past three percent, the highest ever recorded. Five days later they were essentially zero.

show.event: a date axis draws, late December 2024 to late February 2025
the first published point lands: 0.6 percent
the track climbs through 1.8, then 1.2
it peaks in the accent at 3.1 percent and is underlined
a chip lands: Torino 3 - only Apophis ever matched it
the track drops off the bottom of the frame to below 0.1 percent
closer: nobody made a mistake

beats.narration_text: Here is why. The uncertainty is a long thin cloud with Earth inside it. More observations shrink the cloud, so while Earth is still inside, the odds climb. They collapse once the cloud shrinks past us.

show.event: the three target-plane panels land: a terracotta cloud, a fixed ink Earth
labels type in beneath: in the core / on the tail / past the Earth
the computed probability curve draws beneath them, left to right
the peak is marked in ink where the cloud width equals the miss distance
a chip lands in the accent: computed in this reel, not redrawn
closer: a rising number was never bad news

beats.narration_text: Then the same thing happened to the Moon. Its odds climbed for months, to the highest value yet. Webb finally ruled it out in March.

show.event: an ink disc for the Moon, with the same object's track passing it
the lunar figure runs up to 4.3 percent in the accent
a chip: same object, same date, same shape of story
a terracotta cloud shrinks past the Moon and the figure is struck through
a small ink line: ruled out 5 March 2026, from Webb
closer: the shape repeats because the geometry does

beats.narration_text: The tell is this: the learned part answers whether a dot is real. Nothing learned decides whether you should move. And the gap is real - eleven impactors ever caught in advance.

show.event: a card heads WHAT IS ACTUALLY AUTOMATED
row one lands in the accent and is boxed: is this dot real?
row two lands in ink and is STRUCK: should you move?
beside it the completeness bars draw: 1 km done, 140 m at 40%, 30 m barely started
the 90 percent mandate rule lands across them in the accent
a counter: 11 caught before impact, ever
closer: the search is the unfinished part

beats.narration_text: So: the sky is subtracted, the junk is learned away, and the odds come from arithmetic. A rising probability means the cloud is shrinking while we are still inside it.

show.event: the artefact page opens on the cream stage
line one lands
line two lands
line three lands
line four lands in the accent

props.artifactTitle: The Number Went Up - one page
props.artifactHeading: What is learned, and what is not
artifactLines: Surveys photograph the whole sky nightly and subtract; about 100,000 candidate alerts come out.
A CNN sorts eight kinds of dot, then a second net scores four-in-a-row. Human screening fell 90%.
The impact probability is not learned. It is sampled from every orbit the data still permits.
So the number rises while Earth sits in a shrinking cloud - and that is the system working.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Read it: help me tell apart a number that rose because things got worse, from one that rose because the uncertainty shrank, and what to ask before reacting to either. Run that on a forecast you actually track. Watch whether it asks what is shrinking.

show.event: the composer returns, greeting fixed to Your turn.
the prompt types itself in as it is read aloud
terracotta running indicator: paste this into Claude...
three grading lines stagger in as the rubric is spoken

props.command: Help me tell apart a number that rose because the situation got worse, from one that rose because the uncertainty shrank - and tell me what to ask before I react to either.
output: grade it: does it separate the ESTIMATE from the UNCERTAINTY
grade it: does it ask WHAT NEW DATA ARRIVED
grade it: does it name what would make the number FALL

beats.narration_text: The Number Went Up. Humanitarians AI. AI in Astronomy, episode eight.

show.event: the title restates, poster-style, with the terracotta period
a terracotta rule, then the handle
the series subline settles
